16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T46f,LightningLM 0.1V is a recurrence-backbone language-model family grown in four stages: a 1.78B dense seed, then 5B and 9B MoE stages, and finally a 118.67B sparse MoE. The largest model uses 460 routed experts with top-12 routing, and activates 5.93B parameters per token path, roughly five percent of the stored parameters. Each stage is initialized from the previous trained model. The paper emphasizes preserving the learned interfaces during growth, rather than treating expansion as a mostly random reinitialization. Two supporting design choices matter for the memory budget. The model uses BrahmicTokenizer-131K, a 131,072-token byte-level BPE tokenizer, and replaces a conventional learned embedding table with a Kronecker input embedding. A standard lookup table at this vocabulary and width would require about 537M trainable parameters. The Kronecker projection uses about 33.55M trainable parameters and constructs embeddings from frozen byte and position bases through a trained projection. It also avoids materializing a reconstruction table that would otherwise occupy about 2.15GB per GPU, or about 17GB across the node.18:T413,FOGO combines two mechanisms. First, it spectrally orthogonalizes the momentum matrix: for matrix-valued parameters, it approximates the SVD of the momentum B_t and uses the polar factor U_t V_t^T as the update, flattening the singular spectrum so that a few dominant modes do not monopolize optimization. This inherits from Muon's matrix orthogonalization, but FOGO ties it to a unified forgetting interpretation. Second, it maintains a directional memory via random projection: high-dimensional gradients are projected with a Rademacher matrix into a low-dimensional space where pairwise distances are approximately preserved by the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma; representative past directions are stored as centroids in a compact codebook, and new updates are corrected by lightweight orthogonalization in projected space before a proximal step maps them back to parameter space. Compared with OGD-style methods that store past directions in parameter space, FOGO has much lower storage and per-step cost, making it scalable to large models.19:T85f,方法核心是 OPDLM 和其中的 On-Policy Distillation。学生模型来自一个 ARLM checkpoint，但把 causal attention 改成 bidirectional attention，使其可以对被 mask 的任意位置做条件建模。教师模型则保留原始冻结 ARLM。关键难点在于，AR teacher 和 DLM student 的状态空间不同：teacher 习惯在完整左前缀上做 next-token prediction，student 则在部分已知、部分 mask 的序列状态上做去噪。作者的处理方式不是把 teacher 直接搬到随机 mask 状态上，而是让 student 先按自己的 diffusion 解码策略 rollout 出一条反向去噪轨迹，从中采样一个部分去噪状态 x_t，再对其中仍被 mask 的位置做蒸馏。

蒸馏目标的构造很讲究。对每个 masked 位置 i，student 输出该位置的 token 分布；teacher 则读取终态序列 x_0 中该位置之前的 causal prefix，给出 AR 条件分布，作为该位置的监督信号。也就是说，teacher 提供的是“如果按 AR 方式生成到这里，应该偏向哪些 token”，student 学的是“在当前部分去噪状态下，对这些尚未恢复的位置给出与 teacher 一致的分布”。这样做同时解决两件事：一是知识保留，因为监督直接来自原 AR 模型的 logits，而不是只靠 diffusion NELBO 重新学；二是 train-test mismatch，因为训练样本来自 student 自己的 on-policy rollout，而不是离线随机 mask。

论文还加入 rollout-length curriculum。直觉上，训练初期学生模型还不稳定，如果一开始就在很长的去噪轨迹上做 on-policy 学习，状态分布会太差，蒸馏信号也更噪。于是作者逐步增加 rollout 长度，让学生先在较短、较容易的轨迹上对齐，再扩展到更接近真实推理的状态。这个设计和序列决策里的 curriculum / DAGGER 风格很接近，但这里的监督源是冻结 AR teacher。另一个值得注意的点是，作者把 OPDLM 明确定位成 general-purpose DLM 和 task-specific DLM 两种用法：既可以把通用 AR 基座转成通用 DLM，也可以在特定任务上做更便宜的转换。1a:T802,The central idea is OPDLM, trained with On-Policy Distillation. The student starts from an ARLM checkpoint whose causal attention is replaced with bidirectional attention, enabling denoising over arbitrary masked positions. The teacher is the original frozen ARLM. The main challenge is that the teacher and student do not share the same state space: the teacher predicts the next token from a causal prefix, while the student denoises partially observed sequences.

The paper resolves this by letting the student generate its own reverse denoising trajectories. At each training step, the student rolls out a trajectory under its own diffusion decoding policy, and one partially denoised state x_t is sampled from that trajectory. Distillation is then applied only to the still-masked positions in x_t. For each masked position i, the student predicts a token distribution conditioned on the partially denoised sequence, while the teacher provides target logits conditioned on the causal prefix of the terminal sequence x_0 up to position i. In effect, the teacher says what an AR model would prefer at that position, and the student learns to match that preference on the states it will actually encounter during inference.

This design addresses both mismatches at once. Knowledge retention improves because supervision comes directly from the original AR teacher rather than from relearning everything through a diffusion NELBO. Train–test mismatch is reduced because training states are on-policy student states, not uniformly random masks. The paper also introduces a rollout-length curriculum: early in training, the student is supervised on shorter and easier trajectories, and the rollout horizon is gradually increased as the model stabilizes. That choice is important for optimization, since long on-policy trajectories from an immature student would otherwise create noisy and low-quality supervision. The framework is presented both as a general-purpose AR-to-DLM conversion method and as a cheaper task-specific DLM adaptation method.1b:T597,The most informative results are about efficiency and the necessity of on-policy training. On efficiency, the headline number is striking: OPDLM-8B uses only 0.066B training tokens and 4.2 × 10^18 FLOPs, while establishing a new known Pareto frontier on AIME-24. Relative to prior DLM or AR-to-DLM conversion systems such as LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B, SDAR-8B, and Fast-dLLM-v2-7B, the required training tokens are reduced by roughly 15× to 7,000×. That is not a marginal saving; it turns conversion into something much closer to heavy post-training than continued pretraining.

On task performance, the paper evaluates across general-purpose and reasoning-heavy settings, including math and coding, and also studies task-specific conversion. The emphasis is not on claiming the single best absolute score everywhere, but on maintaining strong performance under dramatically lower training cost. The key ablation compares on-policy and off-policy distillation, and on-policy consistently wins, directly supporting the train–inference mismatch argument. Additional appendices study smaller-scale settings, the effect of teacher size, multi-seed evaluation on GPQA-Diamond and AIME variants, and comparisons against standard supervised fine-tuning. The inference section also shows that the converted DLM can exploit multi-token decoding, so the method is not merely changing the training loss while keeping AR-like inference behavior.1c:T527,Read it in the order of problem setup, method, efficiency evidence, and ablations. Start with the introduction and Figure 1 to understand that the paper is about two mismatches in AR-to-DLM conversion, not generic distillation. Then focus on Section 4. Sections 4.1 and 4.2 are the core: 4.1 explains why standard DLM training does not match inference-time states, and 4.2 defines how AR teacher supervision is projected onto those on-policy student states. Section 4.3 on rollout-length curriculum is also worth careful reading because it is likely important for stability. In the experiments, prioritize Sections 5.2 and 5.3: the former tests whether the method works as a general-purpose DLM conversion recipe, and the latter shows why on-policy distillation matters. Then read 5.4 for the practical value of multi-token decoding, and 5.5 for the task-specific setting. In the appendix, A.2, A.4, and A.5 are especially useful for understanding teacher-size dependence, variance across seeds, and the boundary between this method and ordinary SFT. A good question to keep in mind while reading is whether an AR teacher can cap the student’s ceiling. The paper’s answer is pragmatic: first preserve the AR model’s competence under the new bidirectional denoising regime, then benefit from the DLM decoding form.1d:T5af,WAV v1 is a lightweight extension of Block AttnRes. In Block AttnRes, each block stores only a summary C_b, the sum of all residual updates inside the block. WAV v1 keeps this summary and adds two zero-sum detail bases. The first is a phase basis, D_phase, defined by the signed difference between attention and MLP updates, capturing whether the block is more attention-dominant or MLP-dominant. The second is a split basis, D_split, defined by the signed difference between the first-half and second-half updates in the block, capturing coarse early-versus-late directional change. This gives each block not only a total displacement but also two cheap descriptors of its internal trajectory shape. The stabilization choices are conservative. Detail sources are initialized with a negative routing bias, beta_D = -2.0, so the model starts close to Block AttnRes and only uses details when useful. Detail tensors are RMS-matched to the corresponding block summary and clipped by a maximum scale factor rho, preventing them from dominating merely due to larger raw scale. The final prediction mixer does not read detail sources by default; they are used only in intermediate routing. The attention, MLP, embeddings, and output head remain unchanged. Computationally, the number of routing sources grows from about O(N) block summaries to about O(3N) block-basis sources, still block-level rather than layer-level, and the parameter overhead is negligible.1e:T4b5,CHIAR-Former is a 4-layer hybrid transformer. For each token, the model computes spectral entropy from the DCT power spectrum of its representation and routes the token to one of three operators: DCT spectral mixing, RBF kernel mixing, or full self-attention. Low-entropy tokens are treated as smooth and sent to DCT mixing. High-entropy tokens are treated as complex and sent to attention. Mid-range tokens are initially assigned to an RBF kernel branch implemented with random Fourier features.

The paper provides a theoretical motivation for this partition: low-entropy tokens admit bounded DCT truncation error, medium-entropy tokens can be handled by kernel approximation, and high-entropy tokens benefit from dynamic cross-token projection. Relative to FNet, the key difference is selective rather than universal spectral mixing. Relative to Mixture-of-Depths or LayerSkip, the model does not skip computation but changes the operator type while preserving depth. The most important technical outcome, however, is that learned routing collapses: the router repeatedly rejects the RBF branch. The authors then embrace that result and build a DCT+Attention-only variant as the effective architecture.1f:T410,The headline number is on WikiText-103: the DCT+Attention variant reaches validation perplexity 36.54 versus 66.6 for a full-attention baseline, while using 62.5% fewer attention FLOPs. If the setup is fully matched, that is a large gain. Because the gain is so large, the first thing to verify is baseline fairness: same parameter budget, same training schedule, same context length, same optimizer, and same data exposure.

The broader experimental claim is more interesting than the single best result. The paper reports evaluations on four datasets and finds a clear operating regime: spectral routing helps more on larger, naturalistic text corpora, but loses to full attention on small datasets and synthetic pattern-matching tasks. That boundary condition is informative. The most important ablations are likely: three-way routing versus DCT+Attention-only, sensitivity to entropy thresholds, and whether routing collapse is stable across seeds and datasets. Without that stability, the architectural conclusion would be much weaker.20:T4fa,PAPO has two main components.

Step-Aware Process Rewards, or SPR, avoids broadcasting the final outcome reward to all intermediate denoising steps. Instead, it computes an immediate reward for each intermediate step based on a single denoising-step prediction, then combines this signal with the final outcome reward. This gives the optimizer a more step-specific learning signal. The design matters because one diffusion denoising step can update many masked positions in parallel, so token-level credit cannot be inherited from AR generation.

Entropy-Guided Historical Re-enactment, or EHR, replaces artificial randomly masked states with real historical states captured during natural rollouts. During training, the method re-enacts these states and samples them according to model uncertainty, using entropy to focus updates on high-information moments. This avoids spending gradients on already settled decisions and keeps the training states faithful to the model’s actual generation process.

At a high level, PAPO is a GRPO-style policy optimization framework adapted to masked diffusion LMs. The key change is not the group-relative reward idea itself, but the alignment of rewards, log-probability evaluation, and state selection with the denoising trajectory.21:T472,The state space is the countable set of all finite token sequences. The forward process starts from a data sequence and randomly drops tokens with a time-dependent rate. The reverse process starts from a reference distribution and grows the sequence through insertion jumps. Using CTMC time reversal, the ideal reverse rate can be written in terms of the forward rate and time marginals; since the marginals are unknown, the work parameterizes the reverse rate with Transformer models and derives an evidence lower bound on the data likelihood. Two reverse parameterizations are proposed. The first models a single insertion event, including the joint distribution over insertion position and vocabulary item, together with the remaining length. This connects directly to earlier insertion transformers. The second uses an independent, per-dimension factorization that allows multiple insertions in one sampling step, trading exactness for parallel generation. The main difference from earlier ILMs is that the insertion order, denoising objective, and sampler are derived from a single CTMC construction rather than specified separately.22:T782,The method, ADAS (Attention-Discounted Adaptive Sampler), keeps the original sampler’s stopping rule and changes only the ranking step used to build the reveal set. It starts from the usual token-wise base score for each masked position, typically the confidence of the top predicted token. Instead of sorting positions independently by that score, ADAS builds the subset greedily. Once some positions have already been selected, each remaining candidate is discounted according to how strongly it attends to those selected positions and how uncertain those selected positions still are. Intuitively, if candidate i depends heavily on an already selected but still fragile position j, then the marginal value of committing i in the same step should be reduced.

The paper frames this as greedy construction under a non-additive subset utility: confidence acts as an individual utility proxy, while attention acts as a pairwise compatibility proxy. This is the key distinction from prior samplers. Top-k, Fast-dLLM, and EB-Sampler differ mostly in their budget constraints: fixed cardinality, confidence threshold, or entropy budget. They do not make the value of adding one position depend on which other positions are already in the subset. ADAS does exactly that, while remaining plug-compatible with all three.

A notable design choice is using attention as the dependency signal instead of explicit search, planning, or a verifier. The reason is practical: attention is already available from a single forward pass, so the method adds almost no modeling complexity. The paper also provides empirical evidence that masked-token self-attention separates dependent from non-dependent pairs in controlled settings. Implementation-wise, ADAS only modifies the greedy subset construction inside each denoising step, which is why it can be inserted into existing samplers with about 3.1% runtime overhead per model forward.23:T6fc,The empirical section addresses two questions: whether joint dependence is a real failure mode, and whether ADAS improves quality in the low-NFE regime where aggressive parallelism matters most.

In the controlled diagnostic, the authors force the model to predict coupled literals jointly. Accuracy drops from 71% to 30%, showing that good marginal predictions do not imply safe joint commitment. They also show that masked-token self-attention differs between dependent and non-dependent token pairs, which supports the use of attention as a discount signal.

The main evaluation uses two MDLMs, LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base, on four benchmarks covering mathematical reasoning and code generation. The comparison is done at matched denoiser-evaluation budgets rather than at a single operating point, which is the right way to evaluate speed-quality tradeoffs. Adding ADAS to Top-k, EB-Sampler, and Fast-dLLM consistently improves performance, especially in the highly parallel low-NFE regime. Averaged across stopping criteria, ADAS improves matched-NFE performance by 9.11 points on LLaDA-8B-Base and 10.46 points on Dream-7B-Base. It yields positive gains on 80 out of 90 matched operating points.

The pattern of gains is also informative. The benefit is strongest when decoding is aggressive and token-wise ranking is most brittle. As NFE increases and decoding becomes more conservative, the advantage shrinks, which is consistent with the paper’s claim that ADAS addresses joint commitment errors rather than the model’s underlying conditional prediction quality. An important experimental choice is that the authors isolate ranking from stopping: they do not jointly tune both, so the observed gains are easier to attribute to dependency-aware subset construction itself.24:T4c7,This is a skim paper, but it is worth a careful read if you are tracking diffusion or masked language modeling beyond autoregressive decoding. Focus on three parts.

First, read the introduction closely. The key idea is not merely “another sampler,” but the separation between stopping rules and subset ranking, and the claim that joint dependence error is the real bottleneck in aggressive parallel decoding.

Second, inspect the controlled diagnostic and the attention analysis. Those sections determine whether the method has a real mechanism behind it. If attention were not predictive of dependency, the whole discounting rule would be much less convincing.

Third, look at the matched-NFE result tables and plots. The important question is whether gains hold across many operating points and multiple samplers, not whether one cherry-picked speed setting improves.

A useful reading lens is to ask whether attention is a sufficiently robust proxy for dependency, or whether this works mainly on structured tasks like reasoning and code. Another good question is whether ADAS could serve as a target or inductive bias for learned unmasking policies. Around 30-45 minutes should be enough to extract the main ideas.25:T6c0,PCAF has two parallel paths. The first is a local parametric causal LM that handles short-range composition and generalization. The second is an associative memory path that stores local causal successor records extracted from the context window. At inference for a position t, the model forms a query from the current context, uses a route to retrieve a bounded set of candidate records from hash buckets or learned semantic partitions, scores only those candidates with a key-query similarity, and converts the retrieved records into a sparse cache distribution over successor tokens.

Three design choices matter. First, the memory stores successor records rather than generic hidden states. This means retrieval directly produces evidence about what token followed a similar context before, making the memory path behave like an internal neural cache. Second, routing comes in two forms: exact context-hash routing and learned semantic routing. Exact routing is precise and cheap but brittle to surface-form mismatch; semantic routing allows hidden-state-near contexts to retrieve one another. Third, the final prediction is a learned mixture between the parametric LM distribution and the cache distribution. The gate lets the model rely on retrieval when the memory hit is informative, and fall back to the parametric path when retrieval is noisy or absent.

Relative to standard attention, PCAF does not compare against every previous token. Relative to recurrent or SSM-style models, it does not force all history through a single compressed state. Relative to external retrieval LMs, it keeps memory construction and access inside the current context window, with bounded top-K retrieval as the main complexity control.26:T59c,The main evaluation is full autoregressive pretraining rather than synthetic recall tasks. The reported datasets are WikiText-103 and PG-19. The main model is about 303M parameters, compared against matched dense Transformer and local-attention baselines. The paper reports lower perplexity for PCAF on both datasets, together with higher token throughput on a TPU v4-32 pod. That combination is important: the method is not presented as a pure systems tradeoff, but as a modeling change that improves quality at similar scale while also reducing effective compute.

The paper also includes smaller 41M-parameter multi-seed studies to isolate the effects of routing, cache capacity, and the learned gate. From the setup, these ablations are the right ones to inspect: whether the gate is necessary to prevent harmful retrieval, how exact routing compares with semantic routing, and how much benefit remains once top-K and memory capacity are varied. There is also RTX 3060 profiling, which is useful because many long-context alternatives look attractive in asymptotic terms but fail to translate into practical throughput.

The full numeric tables are not available in the provided excerpt, so I cannot safely restate exact perplexity or throughput values. The confirmed experimental anchors are: ~303M main models, ~41M controlled models, WikiText-103 and PG-19 for AR pretraining, and hardware measurements on TPU v4-32 and RTX 3060.27:T45f,For a quick read, focus on three things. First, inspect the formal write/read definition in the method section: what exactly is stored in each record, what the route/key/value are, and how candidate records are aggregated into a vocabulary distribution. Second, check how the gate is parameterized and trained, because that determines whether the model can estimate retrieval reliability rather than just interpolate with a fixed coefficient. Third, read the routing ablations carefully. The exact-hash versus semantic-routing comparison is where the paper either justifies the new primitive or collapses into a cache implementation detail.

A practical reading order is: introduction, the method subsection defining the associative memory pipeline, the main perplexity/throughput table, then the routing/gate/capacity ablations, and finally the hardware profiling. Around 30–45 minutes should be enough for a solid skim. If reading more deeply, pay attention to bucket collisions, train–test consistency of memory construction, and whether the gains are likely to survive at larger scales and much longer contexts.28:Tbfc,方法分成 tokenizer 和 foundation model 两层。

先看 UniTok。作者基于 VQ-VAE 做时间序列离散化，但针对 TS 做了几处关键改造。

第一，incremental tokenization property。普通自编码器式 tokenizer 往往需要看到完整序列后才能稳定编码，这和 AR next-token prediction 不兼容。UniTok 要求前缀序列的 token 化结果只依赖当前前缀，不偷看未来。这一点很关键，因为如果 tokenizer 本身破坏因果性，后续 LM 学到的条件分布就不再对应真实在线预测过程。

第二，prefix normalization。时间序列数值尺度无界，直接量化会让 codebook 被幅值主导，跨域泛化也会很差。作者把序列拆成 scale statistics 和 normalized shape 两部分：尺度信息单独编码成离散 token，归一化后的形状部分再交给 VQ tokenizer。这里不是简单全局标准化，而是前缀式归一化，目的是既稳定尺度，又保持增量性质，不让未来统计量泄漏到当前 token。

第三，progressive-resolution causal autoencoder。作者没有把整个序列压成单一粒度 token，而是按感受野分层编码，让不同 token 承担不同时间尺度的信息。并且编码器/解码器是 causal 的，保证 token 与 NTP 对齐。这个设计是在时间序列场景下借鉴图像 tokenizer 的层级表示，但又避免双向编码带来的未来泄漏。

第四，structure-preserving reconstruction loss。若只用点值重建损失，tokenizer 容易学到数值近似，却丢掉趋势、周期、相位等结构。作者因此加入结构保持目标，让离散 token 更忠实地保留时序形态。摘要片段没有完整公式，但从正文描述看，重点是让重建不仅在 point-wise 误差上好，也在 temporal structure 上稳定。

再看 UniTok-FM。作者用现成 LLM 架构直接做 token-level NTP，没有引入专门的 TS backbone。更重要的是预训练上下文构造：不是只喂单条独立序列，而是在一个 context window 里放入多条“动态相似”的序列片段。训练时这种相似性通过从同一长序列抽段来保证；推理时则根据任务构造 prompt。这样做的目的很明确：把 forecasting、generation、classification 都统一成 in-context 条件建模问题。

推理方式也很像语言模型。zero-shot forecasting 和 prompt-boosted forecasting 都是给定上下文后继续 AR 生成未来 token；few-shot generation 是给少量示例后采样新序列；few-shot classification 则比较不同标签条件下 query 序列的条件似然。作者强调这些能力都不需要 task-specific head 或额外微调。

和 Chronos 这类离散化 TS 模型相比，差异主要在三点。其一，不是简单 point-wise uniform binning，而是学习式 tokenizer。其二，不只服务 forecasting，而是把多任务都放进统一 token 接口。其三，预训练上下文不是孤立单序列，而是显式利用相似序列 prompt，去逼近语言模型里的 in-context pattern matching。29:Td4f,The method has two layers: the tokenizer UniTok and the foundation model UniTok-FM.

Start with UniTok. It is built on VQ-VAE, but the paper makes several modifications tailored to time series.

First, incremental tokenization. A standard autoencoding tokenizer often depends on the full sequence, which breaks compatibility with autoregressive next-token prediction. UniTok enforces that the tokenization of a prefix depends only on that prefix, not on future values. This is a central design constraint. Without it, the downstream LM would be trained on tokens that already leak future information.

Second, prefix normalization. Raw time series can vary wildly in scale, and naive quantization would let magnitude dominate the codebook and hurt cross-domain transfer. The paper decomposes each series into scale statistics and a normalized shape component. Scale is encoded separately into discrete tokens, while the normalized series is passed to the learned tokenizer. Importantly, the normalization is prefix-based rather than global, so it stabilizes scale without violating causality.

Third, a progressive-resolution causal autoencoder. Instead of compressing the series into a single granularity of tokens, the model allocates token resolution according to receptive field, so different tokens capture information at different temporal scales. The encoder and decoder are causal, which keeps the token stream aligned with autoregressive prediction. This borrows the spirit of hierarchical image tokenizers but avoids bidirectional leakage.

Fourth, a structure-preserving reconstruction loss. Pointwise reconstruction alone is not enough for time series because it can preserve local values while losing trend, periodicity, phase, or other temporal structure. The paper therefore adds a reconstruction objective that better preserves sequence structure. The full formula is not visible in the provided excerpt, but the intent is clear: the tokenizer should preserve temporal shape, not just numeric proximity.

On top of UniTok, UniTok-FM uses an off-the-shelf LLM architecture with plain token-level next-token prediction. No time-series-specific backbone is required. A notable design choice is the pretraining context construction: instead of training on isolated single series, the model sees context windows containing multiple series with similar dynamics. During pretraining, similarity is induced by sampling segments from the same long series; at inference time, prompts are assembled according to the task. This is how the paper tries to turn forecasting, generation, and classification into a unified in-context conditional modeling problem.

Inference mirrors language-model usage. Zero-shot forecasting and prompt-boosted forecasting are done by autoregressively generating future tokens from a context. Few-shot generation samples new series conditioned on a few examples. Few-shot classification is done by comparing conditional likelihoods under different label-conditioned prompts. The key claim is that these tasks do not require task-specific heads or fine-tuning.

Compared with Chronos-style discretized TS models, the differences are substantial: learned tokenization instead of simple pointwise uniform binning, a unified interface for multiple tasks rather than forecasting only, and multi-series context construction that explicitly encourages in-context pattern matching.2a:T6d7,The empirical message is straightforward. UniTok-FM is not presented as a specialist model that wins every benchmark. The claim is that a single unified model, without task-specific heads and relying mainly on in-context inference, can cover multiple time-series tasks with competitive performance.

The paper highlights three result categories. First, on forecasting, the unified model matches Chronos-Bolt, a forecasting-oriented TS foundation model. The significance is not absolute dominance but showing that discrete-token NTP is viable for serious forecasting. Second, on generation, few-shot generation quality is reported to be comparable to Diffusion-TS, even though Diffusion-TS is a dedicated generative model. Third, on classification, few-shot in-context classification reaches the level of methods like MOMENT that rely on downstream classifiers.

From a methodology standpoint, the most important evidence is likely in the tokenizer ablations rather than the main leaderboard tables. The critical components to inspect are prefix normalization, the progressive-resolution causal architecture, the structure-preserving loss, and the multi-series context pretraining strategy. If those ablations are strong, they support the paper’s main thesis that the discrete interface design is what makes NTP transfer to time series.

The provided full-content excerpt does not include complete tables, model sizes, training-token counts, codebook sizes, or exact gains, so I cannot safely restate precise numbers. What is clear is that the model is trained on large-scale cross-domain data, and that the comparison to Diffusion-TS should be read mainly as a capability comparison for a unified model rather than a strictly budget-matched contest.2b:T554,This deserves a bit more than a quick skim, around 30 to 45 minutes. The best reading order is to first understand why tokenization is the bottleneck, then inspect how the paper solves it.

Start with the introduction and keep the unification target in mind: forecasting, generation, and classification are all supposed to fit into one NTP framework. Then go straight to the UniTok section and focus on four design choices: incremental tokenization, prefix normalization, the progressive-resolution causal autoencoder, and the structure-preserving loss. That is the most relevant part for pretraining researchers because it addresses how a continuous modality can be converted into an LM-friendly discrete interface.

Next, read the UniTok-FM pretraining setup, especially why the context window contains multiple similar series rather than a single isolated sequence. Finally, check the three task families and the ablations to judge whether the interface is genuinely general-purpose or mainly forecasting-friendly.

If your work touches speech tokenization, visual tokenizers, or unified multimodal LMs, two questions are worth digging into: whether the scale-vs-shape decomposition can transfer to other continuous modalities, and whether progressive-resolution causal tokenization is a modality-general design pattern rather than a time-series-specific trick.2c:T990,论文围绕 WINO 做系统复评。WINO 的思路是：先用 confidence-based adaptive unmasking 逐步生成 token，再根据已生成 token 在当前上下文下的置信度，把低置信 token 重新 mask，给模型一次改写机会。作者没有提出新 remasking 规则，而是把问题拆成三个层次来检查。

第一层是公平比较。作者指出，早期 WINO 结果缺少一个关键 baseline：强 confidence-based unmasking 本身，例如 Fast-dLLM。若不和这种强基线比较，很容易把“更聪明地决定先解哪些 token”带来的收益误记到 remasking 头上。于是论文在相同模型、相同解码预算下，直接比较 Fast-dLLM 与 Fast-dLLM+WINO，考察 remasking 的边际贡献。

第二层是机制诊断。作者追问：为什么 remasking 常常没用？他们的解释不是 remasking 选错了位置，而是更深一层——模型在这些被挑出来重做的位置上，往往提不出比原 token 更好的候选。也就是说，confidence 能发现“不太确定”，却不等于模型具备“重新采样后会更好”的能力。对于 absorbing masked diffusion，这个问题尤其自然，因为训练过程只学习从部分 mask 状态恢复原 token，并没有显式训练“撤销已作决定并在更完整上下文下重选”的行为。

第三层是解码条件依赖性。作者把评估扩展到 stochastic generation，考察温度采样、不同 block size、以及 learned Bernoulli unmasking policy。这里的核心观察是：remasking 的效果高度依赖 unmasking policy。若底层 unmasking 已经是偏确定性的 confidence policy，remasking 的空间很小；若 unmasking policy 本身更随机、更容易引入局部错误，remasking 才更可能修正这些错误。相应地，WINO 在 learned Bernoulli policy 上的收益明显大于在 deterministic Fast-dLLM 上的收益。

这篇论文还有一个重要点是把质量和多样性一起看。作者指出，confidence-based unmasking 已被发现会导致 diversity collapse，而 remasking 在 stochastic setting 下虽然能提高 pass@1，减少部分随机错误，但会进一步压缩样本多样性。也就是说，它改善的是单样本命中率，不一定改善采样分布质量。这个取舍对 diffusion LM 很关键，因为并行生成的一个卖点就是在给定延迟下提供更灵活的采样，而不是把输出进一步推向近似贪心。2d:T883,实验部分的主线很清楚：重新比较 WINO 与强基线，并把评估从标准 greedy 扩展到 stochastic decoding。

在标准采样设置下，也就是短 block length、greedy decoding 或接近确定性的解码条件，WINO 与 Fast-dLLM 基本持平。作者的结论不是“完全无效”，而是“边际收益可以忽略，尤其一旦把 remasking 带来的额外 latency 算进去”。这点很重要，因为 diffusion LM 的核心卖点之一就是吞吐和并行度；如果一个修正机制带来额外步数，却没有换来稳定质量提升，那它在系统层面就站不住。

机制实验进一步支持上述判断。作者检查了被 remask 的位置在下一轮是否真的会被替换成更优 token，发现很多情况下模型并不能提出更好的替代项。这说明瓶颈不在 confidence estimator，而在底层 reverse model 的条件建模能力。换句话说，remasking 只是在暴露模型不会 revision，而不是自动赋予 revision 能力。

在 stochastic generation 下，结果更复杂。使用非零温度时，WINO 可以修复一部分采样噪声导致的错误，因此 pass@1 有提升；但与此同时，多样性下降更明显，延续并加重了 confidence-based unmasking 已知的 diversity collapse。这个现象说明 remasking 更像一个“去随机化”装置：它能把明显偏离高概率模式的 token 拉回来，但代价是样本分布更窄。

当 WINO 与 learned Bernoulli unmasking policy 结合时，收益明显大于与 deterministic Fast-dLLM 结合时。作者据此认为，remasking 的有效性不能脱离 unmasking policy 单独讨论。若前者是后验修正，后者决定了前面到底制造了多少可修正错误。

从全文节选里看不到完整的模型参数量、数据规模和所有具体数字表格，因此不能在这里可靠填入精确百分比或延迟倍数。但论文给出的定性结论很稳：1）标准 greedy/短块设置下，WINO 对强基线几乎没有净增益；2）随机采样下，pass@1 可能提升，但多样性进一步塌缩；3）在 learned Bernoulli policy 上，remasking 的边际价值显著更大。2e:T483,This matters a lot for alternative language modeling paradigms, especially masked diffusion and related any-order generation. The value of the paper is not a new algorithm but a correction to an emerging narrative: masked dLLMs do not become reliably self-correcting just by adding a training-free remasking heuristic. The key point is that remasking only helps if the underlying model can actually propose a better replacement token after the position is masked again. If the reverse model lacks that conditional revision ability, remasking mostly adds steps without adding quality. For pretraining research, the implication is direct: if we want diffusion LMs to support robust revision, that ability may need to be built into the training objective, the forward process, the decoding policy, or post-training, rather than assumed to emerge from a post-hoc heuristic.

The contribution is mainly careful re-evaluation and mechanism clarification. It is not a paradigm shift by itself, but it should change how future papers choose baselines, report latency-quality tradeoffs, and reason about whether revision should be learned or decoded heuristically.2f:Ta49,The paper performs a systematic re-evaluation of WINO. WINO works by combining confidence-based adaptive unmasking with a confidence-based remasking step: after some tokens have been generated, low-confidence decoded tokens are masked again so the model gets another chance to fill them in. The authors do not propose a new remasking rule. Instead, they decompose the question into three layers.

First, they enforce a fair comparison. They argue that earlier WINO evaluations missed the most important baseline: strong confidence-based unmasking on its own, such as Fast-dLLM. Without that baseline, gains from better unmasking order can be mistakenly attributed to remasking. So the paper compares Fast-dLLM directly against Fast-dLLM+WINO under matched model and decoding budgets, isolating the marginal value of remasking.

Second, they diagnose the mechanism. Why does remasking often fail to help? Their answer is not merely that the wrong positions are selected. The deeper issue is that, at many remasked positions, the model cannot produce a better alternative token than the one it already chose. Confidence can identify uncertainty, but uncertainty does not imply that the model has a superior replacement available. This is especially natural in absorbing masked diffusion, where training teaches the model to reconstruct original tokens from partially masked inputs, but does not explicitly train it to revoke previous decisions and re-decide under richer context.

Third, they study dependence on decoding conditions. The evaluation is extended to stochastic generation, varying temperature, block size, and unmasking policy, including learned Bernoulli unmasking. The central observation is that remasking effectiveness is highly policy-dependent. If the base unmasking policy is already deterministic and confidence-driven, there may be little room left for remasking to improve anything. If the unmasking policy is more stochastic and introduces more local errors, remasking has more opportunities to repair them. Consistent with that view, WINO helps much more on top of learned Bernoulli policies than on top of deterministic Fast-dLLM.

A further strength of the paper is that it evaluates quality and diversity together. Confidence-based unmasking has already been linked to diversity collapse, and the paper shows that remasking can intensify this effect. Under stochastic decoding, WINO may improve pass@1 by correcting some sampling-induced errors, but it also narrows the sample distribution further. So the gain is not a free quality improvement; it is often a trade of diversity for single-sample accuracy.30:T9a7,The experimental story is clean: re-compare WINO against a strong baseline, then extend the evaluation from standard greedy decoding to stochastic generation.

Under standard sampling settings, meaning short block lengths and greedy or near-deterministic decoding, WINO performs roughly on par with Fast-dLLM. The paper does not claim remasking is universally useless; the claim is narrower and more important: its marginal gain is often negligible once the extra latency from remasking is included. That matters because one of the main motivations for diffusion LMs is throughput and parallelism. If a correction mechanism adds decoding steps without delivering stable quality gains, it weakens the systems case for using it.

The mechanism analysis supports this conclusion. The authors inspect whether remasked positions are actually replaced by better tokens in subsequent steps and find that this often does not happen. That points to a limitation of the underlying reverse model rather than the confidence estimator. In other words, remasking exposes the absence of revision ability; it does not create that ability.

Under stochastic generation, the picture becomes more nuanced. At non-zero temperature, WINO can repair some errors introduced by sampling noise, so pass@1 improves. But diversity drops further, extending and worsening the diversity collapse already known for confidence-based unmasking. This suggests that remasking often acts as a de-randomization mechanism: it pulls samples back toward high-probability modes, which helps single-sample accuracy but narrows the output distribution.

When WINO is paired with learned Bernoulli unmasking policies, the gains are meaningfully larger than when it is paired with deterministic Fast-dLLM. The paper therefore argues that remasking cannot be evaluated in isolation from the unmasking policy. The latter determines how many correctable mistakes are created upstream.

The excerpt provided here does not include the full parameter counts, data scales, or all numeric tables, so I cannot safely reproduce exact percentages or latency multipliers. But the qualitative findings are clear and stable: (1) under standard greedy/short-block settings, WINO adds little over a strong confidence-based baseline; (2) under stochastic decoding, pass@1 can improve while diversity collapses further; and (3) remasking is substantially more useful with learned Bernoulli unmasking than with deterministic Fast-dLLM.31:T5f0,This one is worth a careful read. 第二层是 AGDO 框架。核心做法是先从 valid attention score 中构造 attention-guided denoising order，再把这个顺序用于 post-training。这里的 valid attention 可以理解为：只统计指向当前可见、已解码或未被 mask 的上下文 token 的注意力，从而估计某个 masked token 当前是否已经拥有足够支撑它被恢复的上下文。AGDO 不是按固定位置顺序解码，也不是简单 blockwise，而是按 attention 支撑度决定谁先被 unmask。

在 RL 阶段，AGDO-RL 建立在已有 dLLM 的 GRPO/mean-field 近似路线之上，但同样把 attention-guided order 和 token reweighting 纳入优化。也就是说，它不是只在 sample-level 上根据最终 reward 调整，而是让 credit assignment 更偏向那些对后续推理链条更关键的 token。和 diff-GRPO、wd1 这类方法相比，区别不在 RL 框架本身，而在于它把 policy optimization 的作用位置从“随机选中的 masked token”改成了“按 attention 依赖组织起来的 token 子集”。36:T71e,The method has two layers. First is an empirical attention study. On Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, the authors trace final-layer attention along the denoising trajectory and report two main findings: attention is sparse and temporally stable across steps, and tokens that place more attention mass on already-denoised context exhibit more stable generation probabilities. This suggests that masked tokens are not equally predictable at a given step, which directly challenges fully random masking.

Second is AGDO, an attention-guided denoising and optimization framework. It derives an attention-guided denoising order from valid attention scores, where the key idea is to estimate whether a masked token already has enough support from currently visible or denoised context. Instead of decoding by position or by random selection, AGDO unmasks tokens according to attention-supported readiness.

AGDO-SFT uses this order during supervised fine-tuning, reducing the mismatch between training and inference trajectories. On top of that, it introduces attention-based reweighting: tokens that act more like attention hubs receive larger loss weights because mistakes on them are more likely to propagate through later denoising steps.

AGDO-RL extends the same principle to reinforcement learning. It stays within the recent dLLM RL line based on GRPO-style optimization with mean-field approximations, but changes where optimization pressure is applied. Rather than treating randomly masked positions as the optimization target, it organizes token-level credit assignment around attention-induced dependencies and emphasizes attention-critical tokens. Relative to methods like diff-GRPO or wd1, the novelty is less about the RL backbone and more about aligning policy optimization with the model’s intrinsic denoising structure.37:T5c7,From the provided full text, the experimental focus is on math and coding reasoning benchmarks, with the main claim being consistent gains over random-masking post-training baselines and over externally imposed decoding orders. First, the paper reformulates attention approximation in terms of softmax KDE. This is natural because attention weights are normalized exponential kernels between queries and keys. Once written this way, the problem can be attacked using tools from coresets, polynomial approximation, high-dimensional geometry, and communication complexity.

Second, the analysis is split by regime. The table of contents makes clear that the authors treat a high-temperature regime and a low-temperature regime separately. Intuitively, when temperature is high, softmax is smoother and more amenable to low-degree approximation; when temperature is low, the kernel becomes sharper, local geometry matters more, and compression becomes harder. The paper therefore avoids a single coarse statement and instead derives regime-specific upper and lower bounds.

Third, the upper and lower bounds use different toolchains. On the upper-bound side, the paper employs multivariate polynomial methods, Hermite polynomials, KDE coresets, and a merge-and-reduce style conversion from offline compression to streaming compression. In the low-temperature regime, the contents indicate a more delicate pipeline: partition the dataset into pseudo-random and low-radius components, recenter and rescale them, build coresets for each part, then turn the offline compressor into a streaming algorithm. This suggests that the main technical novelty lies in decomposing the geometry of the instance before compressing it.

On the lower-bound side, the paper uses information-theoretic and communication-complexity arguments to show that some memory requirements are inherent rather than artifacts of loose analysis. The final section transfers the softmax-KDE results back to attention, yielding formal bounds for streaming attention itself.

A skim should take about 25–40 minutes. A full proof read will take much longer. It is helpful to keep the earlier papers by Haris et al. and Kochetkova et al. nearby and compare exactly where the new bounds become tighter.41:T836,OffQ has a simple three-stage logic: identify the outlier direction, concentrate outlier energy into very few channels, then convert that energy into offsets that can be absorbed by the quantizer zero-point.

First, it identifies a low-dimensional outlier subspace using a tailored top-1 PCA procedure. The motivation comes from recent observations that high-norm activation outliers share similar directions across layers, token identities, and sequence positions. Instead of expensive full PCA or learned transformations, OffQ extracts the dominant outlier direction with a lightweight top-1 procedure.

Second, it applies an orthonormal rotation so that large-magnitude activations are concentrated into one or a few channels. This is related to rotation-based methods such as QuaRot and SpinQuant, but the goal is different. Those methods mainly try to spread energy and make the distribution more Gaussian-like. OffQ explicitly tries to gather structured outlier mass into a minimal set of channels so that it can be removed cleanly afterward.

Third, it performs group-wise offset absorption. Channels are reordered into groups, each assigned one outlier channel. A specialized Hadamard rotation is then applied within each group to transform the outlier energy into a shared offset. That offset is absorbed into the zero-point of standard low-bit quantization. Intuitively, instead of forcing the quantizer to represent a very large outlier channel directly, the method rewrites its effect as a group-level baseline shift. The remaining values then have much smaller variance and can be quantized more accurately.

The design choices are important. It keeps uniform quantization rather than switching to non-uniform codebooks, which helps hardware compatibility. It avoids mixed precision, so execution remains homogeneous. It also avoids backpropagation-based rotation learning, reducing calibration cost and implementation burden. The main assumption is that outliers are indeed low-dimensional and directionally stable; if that structure breaks, top-1 concentration may become less effective.42:T645,The paper focuses on the difficult W4A4KV4 setting, where weights, activations, and KV cache are all quantized to 4 bits. This is a much stronger test than weight-only quantization and is the right place to evaluate whether outlier handling is genuinely effective.
